extra_misconceptions.fact: Heat or suffocation causes the tick to regurgitate infectious fluids into the wound; pull it straight out with fine tweezers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying a lit match or petroleum jelly to an embedded tick forces it to back out safely without leaving mouthparts.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Incising and sucking a snakebite damages tissue and causes infection without removing venom; keep the limb still at heart level.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cutting a pit viper bite and sucking out the venom reduces the amount of toxin entering the victim's bloodstream.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Alcohol dilates surface blood vessels and accelerates heat loss from the core; give warm, sweet, non-caffeinated liquids instead.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Giving alcohol or caffeinated hot drinks to a shivering hiker warms their core and prevents worsening hypothermia.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rubbing embeds sharp particles into the cornea and causes abrasions; flush the eye gently with clean water or sterile saline.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rubbing a gritty eye after windblown dust enters the eyelid helps flush the foreign particle toward the tear duct.

extra_socratic_questions: Which physical indicator distinguishes life-threatening heatstroke from heat exhaustion during a desert hike?
Why is it dangerous to pop an intact friction blister with an unsterilized pocketknife on a multi-day trek?
What happens to core body temperature when a hypothermia victim is placed directly into a hot bath too quickly?
Under what condition does an ankle injury require full immobilization and litter evacuation rather than taping?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Food is the seventh and lowest survival priority because a healthy person can survive weeks without eating if kept warm and hydrated.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Finding edible wild plants and hunting game should be your first priority during the initial twenty-four hours lost.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hypothermia can kill in a few hours of cold rain or wind, whereas dehydration takes several days to become life-threatening.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Locating a clean water source comes before shelter and fire whenever a hiker becomes stranded in mountain terrain.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Signaling ranks fifth right after shelter and fire because attracting early search aircraft ends the emergency before supplies run low.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Signaling for rescue should wait until you have established a multi-day base camp with steady food and water supplies.

extra_misconceptions.fact: First aid is the second priority immediately after positive mental attitude because even minor injuries can rapidly disable a solo survivor.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: First aid applies only to major trauma and sits below shelter construction in the seven wilderness survival priorities.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to spend daylight hours foraging for wild food before constructing a weatherproof shelter?
Under what condition does building an emergency shelter take precedence over starting a warming fire at dusk?
What happens to your survival timeline if untreated bleeding or shock is ignored while you search for drinking water?
Where does signaling rank among the seven survival priorities compared to procuring food and purifying stream water?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Blindly rushing increases the distance from your last known point and raises injury risk; stop immediately and apply the S.T.O.P. method.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Running along unblazed game trails as soon as you realize you are off course maximizes your chance of finding the road.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Honest communication and shared tasks build calm teamwork, while secrecy breeds distrust and causes hikers to make poor solo choices.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hiding the severity of a navigation mistake from your patrol members prevents panic and keeps everyone moving faster.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sleep deprivation and physical exhaustion impair prefrontal decision-making and trigger panic; scheduled rest preserves mental clarity.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pushing through exhaustion without rest breaks keeps a lost hiker's mind occupied and prevents fear from setting in.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Productive routines like improving insulation, organizing signal fires, and tending camp provide a sense of control that sustains morale.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sitting idle in camp once basic shelter is finished saves the most mental energy while waiting for search teams.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a lost hiker's energy reserves and judgment when adrenaline triggers an immediate sprint down a trail?
Which step of the S.T.O.P. procedure requires inventorying your remaining daylight, pack gear, and terrain landmarks?
Why is it dangerous to keep walking after sunset in unfamiliar backcountry instead of accepting your current location?
What psychological effect does assigning concrete camp tasks like gathering tinder have on a frightened group at night?

extra_misconceptions.fact: If you lose your pack during a river crossing or slide, a kit inside it is gone; carry core survival items on your person at all times.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Keeping your survival kit buried at the bottom of your expedition pack protects it until you set up evening camp.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Humidity and condensation ruin uncoated match heads; dip matches in melted paraffin or carry stormproof matches and a ferrocerium rod.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard household strike-anywhere matches stay reliable in a pocket survival tin without any waterproof coating.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wet cork or plastic peas freeze solid against the whistle chamber in subfreezing weather; always pack a pealess plastic rescue whistle.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A brass whistle with a cork pea is the best choice for winter survival kits because it projects a louder warbling tone.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unfamiliar tools fail under stress and cold hands; you must personally test every fire starter, blade, and water tablet before a trip.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Buying a pre-packaged commercial survival tin guarantees you are ready for an unexpected night out without field practice.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to store your personal survival kit inside your main backpack rather than on your belt or pockets?
What measurement confirms that heavy-duty contractor trash bags in your survival kit are thick enough for a shelter?
Under what condition does a pealess rescue whistle outperform shouting when trying to alert nearby ground searchers?
Which multi-use item in a compact survival kit allows you to both boil stream water and dig a shallow drainage trench?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Large interior air volume forces your body to heat dead space; a shelter should be just large enough to fit your body plus thick bedding.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Building a tall, spacious A-frame shelter with standing headroom keeps you warmer than a low, tight debris hut.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An unvented snow shelter traps exhaled carbon dioxide and can cause asphyxiation; always poke a fist-sized vent hole through the roof.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sealing every air gap in a snow cave or quinzhee with packed snow maximizes warmth throughout a subzero night.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Direct sun and hot wind accelerate sweat loss and cause solar burns; loose, full-coverage clothing traps humid air and slows dehydration.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Removing your shirt and hat in hot desert conditions helps sweat evaporate faster and conserves your body water.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Shorelines look closer than they are and swimming in cold water rapidly drains body heat; stay with the floating boat and adopt HELP posture.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Abandoning a capsized canoe to swim toward a distant shoreline is safer than staying with the swamped watercraft.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to conductive heat loss if you build a thick debris roof but sleep directly on bare, frozen forest ground?
Where should a Scout position the entrance and ventilation hole when digging a snow cave or trench shelter on a slope?
Why is it dangerous to wear cotton jeans and a cotton hoodie underneath a rain shell during a cold autumn rainstorm?
Under what condition does wearing loose, light-colored long sleeves protect a stranded hiker better than shorts and a tank top?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sparks cool in milliseconds and only ignite high-surface-area fibers like birch bark scrapings, cattail down, or feathered wood curls.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scraping a ferrocerium rod slowly over pencil-thick twigs will ignite a campfire without preparing fibrous fine tinder.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Without an eighth-wedge notch cut to the center of the socket, hot wood dust scatters and cools instead of piling into an insulated ember.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Spinning a bow-drill spindle on a flat, unnotched wooden hearth board produces a glowing coal directly around the socket.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ground wood absorbs soil moisture and rots; snap dead branches off standing trees or split wet logs to expose dry heartwood for feather sticks.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dead branches lying flat on the damp forest floor make the best kindling because they require no cutting or splitting.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Forceful blowing scatters a fragile coal and cools it below ignition point; breathe gently and steadily until smoke turns thick and yellow.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Blowing as hard and fast as possible onto a newly transferred friction coal brings a tinder bundle to flame immediately.

extra_socratic_questions: What ratio of prepared tinder, kindling, and fuel wood should be stacked before you strike a single spark in wet weather?
Where should the V-shaped notch on a bow-drill fireboard be cut so that hot black punk dust collects into a coalescing ember?
Which physical indicator shows that cotton char cloth has finished pyrolyzing inside a tin and is ready to catch a flint spark?
Why is it dangerous to build a survival fire directly against a snow-covered boulder or beneath conifer branches heavy with snow?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Mirror flashes at close range can temporarily blind the pilot during critical maneuvers; stop flashing once the aircraft acknowledges you.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Flashing a signal mirror continuously at a rescue helicopter cockpit during its final landing approach helps the pilot touch down.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ground-to-air symbols must be at least ten to eighteen feet long with high-contrast trenches or dark branches to be legible from the air.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Stomping a two-foot-tall letter V into shallow snow creates a ground-to-air symbol that search planes can read from altitude.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Three evenly spaced blasts, flashes, or fires separated by pauses form the universal distress signal recognized by search and rescue teams.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Firing or blowing a single long whistle blast every few minutes is the international distress pattern for wilderness rescue.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dense smoke is invisible at night and smothers bright flames; use dry, resinous wood for a bright night fire and save green foliage for day.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Piling wet leaves onto a signal fire at night makes it easier for search aircraft to spot your position in the dark.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a Scout position the V-finger aiming sight when flashing a signal mirror without a built-in retroreflective window?
What happens to the visibility of a signal fire during bright midday sun if you burn only dry hardwood instead of green boughs?
Which ground-to-air symbol tells an overhead rescue helicopter pilot that a member of your group requires urgent medical evacuation?
Why is it dangerous to lay out ground-to-air distress symbols inside a narrow canyon floor or beneath dense forest canopy?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Even crystal-clear mountain streams can carry Giardia and Cryptosporidium cysts from wildlife upstream; always treat backcountry water.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Clear, fast-moving alpine stream water above timberline is naturally pure and safe to drink without boiling or treatment.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pasteurization occurs below boiling, and bringing water to a full rolling boil for one minute kills bacteria, viruses, and protozoan cysts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Water must be kept at a vigorous rolling boil for at least twenty minutes at high altitude to destroy waterborne bacteria.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Iodine is ineffective against Cryptosporidium; use boiling, a 1-micron absolute filter, or chlorine dioxide with extended four-hour contact.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard iodine tablets kill hard-shelled Cryptosporidium oocysts within thirty minutes in cold backcountry lakes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Untreated droplets in the threads can infect you; loosen the cap and invert the bottle so treated water rinses the threads before waiting.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sealing a water bottle tightly right after dropping in a chemical tablet disinfects the bottle threads and cap interior.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the required contact time of chemical water tablets when you treat icy glacial meltwater near freezing?
Why is it dangerous to add iodine or chlorine tablets to muddy creek water without first filtering out suspended sediment?
What measurement confirms that stream water heated in a metal cup has reached a full rolling boil sufficient to kill pathogens?
Under what condition does a standard 0.2-micron hollow-fiber microfilter fail to make contaminated backcountry water safe?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Birds and rodents metabolize many plant alkaloids and fungal amatoxins that cause fatal liver or kidney failure in humans.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wild berries and mushrooms that birds or squirrels eat safely in the forest are also safe for humans to consume.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cooking kills bacteria and parasites in meat, but heat does not destroy deadly chemical compounds in hemlock or death cap fungi.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Boiling unknown wild plants or game meat for twenty minutes neutralizes all plant toxins and bacterial hazards.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Healthy humans can survive up to three weeks without food, so conserving energy, staying warm, and finding water take priority.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hunting small game and foraging for wild roots should begin on the first day a hiker becomes lost in the woods.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Digesting protein consumes metabolic water from body tissues, and eating unmelted snow lowers core temperature and worsens cold stress.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Eating snow or raw high-protein insect larvae helps a dehydrated survivor restore energy and moisture at the same time.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your body's water reserves when digesting high-protein wild game without an abundant supply of drinking water?
Which physical indicator separates edible Queen Anne's lace from deadly poison hemlock, and why is field identification risky?
What caloric deficit occurs when a lost hiker spends four hours setting snares instead of resting inside an insulated shelter?
Why is it dangerous to test unfamiliar berries in the backcountry when a single bout of vomiting can trigger severe dehydration?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Federal protection rangers must also complete seasonal law enforcement academy training, medical certification, and pack fitness tests.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A four-year forestry degree alone qualifies an applicant to work immediately as a backcountry law enforcement park ranger.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Mountain and wilderness search and rescue in the United States relies primarily on trained unpaid volunteers coordinated by sheriffs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Most county search and rescue team members are full-time paid employees who receive a regular government salary for rescues.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Professional guides typically need Wilderness First Responder or Wilderness EMT credentials to manage patients hours from hospital care.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard urban CPR and basic first aid cards meet the medical training requirements for professional wilderness expedition guides.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Volunteers usually purchase and maintain their own personal 24-hour field pack, footwear, and layers before joining active callouts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Volunteer search and rescue agencies supply every piece of personal clothing, boots, and navigation gear for new field members.

extra_socratic_questions: What steps should you take before interviewing a search and rescue specialist to ensure parent approval and focused questions?
Which medical scope of practice separates a Wilderness EMT from a basic Wilderness First Aid holder on a backcountry rescue team?
What training hours, recertification fees, and physical fitness benchmarks must you record when comparing two outdoor careers?
Under what condition does a county search and rescue unit require volunteers to carry a self-sufficient 24-hour gear pack?
